Before I go through some of the key findings of this report, I just want to stress one very important point.
The City of Kitchener and indeed our whole community is very fortunate to have a network of volunteer-run
and neighbourhood associations who are interested and skilled in providing programming out of
some of the city's community centres. Programming these centres requires a significant amount
of effort and volunteer hours, and many of those associations are doing great work to
help fill some of the city centres with programming. We are incredibly thankful to all of the volunteers
who put in so many hours to provide vital programming to the residents of Kitchener.
I also want to stress that we're very fortunate to have a team of dedicated and highly skilled
municipal employees who work in the community centres and want to do more to activate their
centres but are constrained by the City's existing policies and procedures.
The challenge before Council today is not with hard-working neighbourhood association
volunteers nor the dedicated staff that work in the City's community centres.
It's with the City's outdated community centre operating model that has not changed
with the times, and it is not meeting the needs of all of Kitchener residents.
The current operating model is based on two key city policies, the facility booking policy
and our Neighbourhood Association Filiation Policy, both of which were approved more than
20 years ago and have not substantially changed since that time despite all the social and
economic changes we've seen in our community. Along with these two
key city policies, the community centre operating model relies heavily on
the association volunteers to do a significant amount of work to provide
programming out of city-owned community centres, putting a burden of work on
volunteers that is much greater than any other Canadian municipality of similar
size. The downward trend in volunteerism we are seeing in our community and
across Canada indicates that reliance on volunteers to program centers is no longer sustainable.
In fact, many neighborhood associations shared that they are struggling to act and retain volunteers.
While this model may be the least expensive for the municipality, it's not the best model for meeting needs of all residents in the community.
It is fair to say that the current operating model is well for some community centers.
However, it is also leaving other centers under-programmed and underutilized.
When we look at all the programming happening in our centers, which includes those offered by the City and Neighbored Association,
55% of all programming is being offered out of just four of our 14 community centers.
This means that residents living in our neighborhoods close to one of those
four community centers are being very well served by the current model.
However, residents living near the 10 centers are not.
Another way to look at how our current operating model is doing is to consider
the number of programs being offered at each center based on income levels of
of the surrounding neighbourhoods.
As this slide illustrates, 68% of all programming is happening at the seven community centres
located in mid- to high-income neighbourhoods, while only 32% of programs are being offered
in the seven centres located in neighbourhoods within a median household income below the
cities.
In other words, residents living in neighbourhoods with lower household incomes have less access
community centre programming near their home than those living in neighbourhoods
with higher household incomes. In addition to looking at the number of
programs being offered at our community centres, staff also looked at the types
of programs being offered. Again, this analysis demonstrates the current
operating model is not meeting the needs of residents. And let me explain. Back in
March of 2022, the city partnered with Envirronics Research to conduct a statistically representative
survey of Kitchener residents on a wide variety of municipal issues, including their priorities
for recreation and leisure programming. The results demonstrated that residents prioritized
recreation and leisure programs that target three key areas, which are shown on this slide.
The top priority was mental health and well-being.
The second priority was services for vulnerable populations.
And the third priority was physical health and fitness.
As this chart illustrates, residents' third priority of physical health and fitness is
being covered very well under the current operating model.
However, residents' first and second priorities for programming are not being adequately addressed,
only 5% of all programming targeting these two priority areas.
In order to begin to modernize the City's current community centre operating model,
staff have put forward a series of recommendations which are summarized on this slide.
This list of potential changes was created according to three main objectives included
in the motion City Council passed unanimously on March 20, 2023.
First, strengthening and modernizing collaborative partnerships
between the city and community partners.
Second, increasing residence usage of city-owned community centers.
And third, diversifying programs and supports
offered out of city-owned community centers.
In drafting these recommendations,
staff worked closely with the management team within the neighborhood programs and services division.
In addition, affiliated neighborhood associations were surveyed to provide input on a number of these potential changes.
All of the association responses we received were considered very carefully by staff,
and several changes, additions, and deletions were made to our recommendations based on their input.
Staff that implementation of any of these ideas, if approved, requires some additional
work by Neighboured Associations.
Staff are committed to support Neighboured Associations in completing this work and heard
from many of the Neighboured Associations through the online survey that the changes
should be phased in over time with plenty of staff support and transparent communication
along the way.
